matt: Heads-up — I ran the nightly fused-attn sweep and saw a reproducible p99 regression (~+4%) on our small-sequence workloads after the kernel-selector change.
matt: Quick summary: long-seq perf unchanged, but seq<=32 bursty requests spike. Baseline (old selector) p99=18ms, new selector p99=18.7ms. Not huge but consistent across GPUs.
tara: hmm. did you check epilogue fusion flags? small-seq tends to mis-pick packed-QKV+epilogue combo sometimes.
matt: Yes — the selector favours pack+epilogue for qkvpack32 on sm75/80. Profiling shows extra memwalks in the epilogue for small lanes. Snippet from nvprof:
```
Memcpy HtoD 2.1ms
FusedAttnEp 0.9ms (lots of device-to-device copies)
KernelSelector: chosen=pack_qkv_epilogue
```
jia: can you paste the perf trace (timeline)? curious if it's latency jitter from L2 thrash or a scheduling preemption.
matt: pasted timeline to thread: <ci/bench/3001/trace>. Looks like multiple tiny kernels are being scheduled instead of a single coalesced path.
nate: any change in the batching heuristic? small-seq workloads rely on continuous batching/aggregation. selector tweak could break the heuristic that merges micro-batches.
matt: batching config unchanged. But selector now has an extra cost-model term that penalizes flop-count for non-packed kernels; appears to push towards epilogue-packed path even when it fragments memory.
tara: proposed quick mitigation: gate epilogue fusion for seq<=48 or when packed-qkv lane_util < 0.4. We can add a cheap heuristic to selector to avoid pack+epilogue for those cases.
jia: agree. Also add a perf-test that samples seq=8/16/32 with burst patterns in CI to catch regressions. Right now we only check average throughput.
matt: created a tiny patch that disables epilogue fusion on small lanes and ran local microbench: p99 back to 18.1ms. I'll open PR with flags + perf-test.
nate: include commit hash from the selector tweak and GPU model in the PR description. I'll help run full-nightly if you need.
matt: PR: https://git.internal/repo/infra/patches/1234 — contains selector-guard + new perf case. patch id=abc1234
perf-bot: nightly-bench: fused-attn small-seq suite queued. results will post to <ci/bench/3001/results> when done :hourglass_flowing_sand:
tara: thanks — if CI still shows a blip, we might consider a more surgical fix in the epilogue write-path (reduce memory copies) instead of heuristic. but heuristics are fine short-term.
matt: agreed. next steps in PR description. I'll merge the guard if CI is green and then profile deeper on the epilogue kernel for root cause. :mag:
jia: nice, thanks for catching this early. saves customers from subtle latency regressions. :thumbsup:
